thread:
tara: Quick flag  PR #910 updates audit export docs. Legal wants clearer wording around TTL scope and redaction examples.

ben: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/910 — looks small.

nina: main ask: label each snippet as either 'tenant-scoped' or 'global/admin' and add a one-line note about scope.

legal-ian: please use this exact SOC2-friendly sentence where we summarize retention: 'Retention settings shown apply to the tenant indicated unless labeled "global/admin". Indefinite retention may be required under legal hold.' Keep it verbatim.

tara: will add that line. Also include a tiny CLI redact example so engineers see default behavior.

ben: proposed snippets: 

```bash
# tenant-scoped: export and redact IP and email
redwood audits export --tenant acme --since 2026-09-01 --redact ip,email
```

```python
# tenant-scoped: set 90-day retention for tenant 'acme'
client.set_audit_retention(tenant_id='acme', ttl_seconds=90*24*3600)  # 90 days (P90D)
# Note: this TTL applies to logs collected for the tenant above.
```

nina: add a one-line parenthetical after the tenant snippet: '(Private/VPC/on-prem deployments may follow customer-managed retention and key policies.)'

legal-ian: also prefer replacing casual words like 'permanent' with 'indefinite retention (subject to legal hold)' when we mention legal-hold edge cases.

tara: noted. I'll push small edits: labeled snippets, SOC2 sentence, CLI redact example, and the private deployment parenthetical.
